title: KV cache healing via generational reservoirs and GPU-aware scavenger
creator: Maya Chen
description: Background: Continuous batching and long-lived chat sessions create highly variable KV cache object size distributions. Small frequent updates (token-level KV writes) intermix with large prefix caches, producing fragmentation in GPU-backed allocations. Existing slab and chunked allocators handle steady-state well but show slow drift in free space patterns, causing out-of-memory tail events and elevated eviction churn.
problem_statement: Design and implement an allocation and background reclamation strategy that reduces KV cache fragmentation without blocking hot inference paths and without degrading continuous-batching latency SLOs. The solution must be GPU-memory-aware, coordinate with batching/fence semantics, and be safe for live rollouts on Dedicated clusters.
goals: Decrease fragmentation-driven OOMs by >= 40% in mixed short/long sequence workloads
Ensure background healing work never adds >1ms median per-request latency during normal traffic
Preserve throughput with <3% throughput regression under 95th percentile load profiles
Integrate with batching fences so reclaim only proceeds when KV references are safe
non_goals: Full rewrite of allocator strategies (keep existing slab/chunk infrastructure)
Moving KV entries between GPUs — cross-device migration is out of scope
acceptance_criteria: Load test: mixed chat + long-context benchmark shows fragmentation metric drop >=40% vs baseline (metric: free-range-count / total-free-memory)
Continuous-batching 95th percentile latency during healing <= baseline + 1ms
No correctness regressions on unit/e2e KV stress tests (coverage for read-after-write and concurrent eviction)
Feature gated behind runtime flag and rolloutable via canary
design_summary: Introduce a generational reservoir model: new allocations are taken from a 'young' micro-pool with tight packing for small objects; objects surviving X compact cycles are promoted to a 'stable' pool optimized for larger allocations. A GPU-aware scavenger thread asynchronously compacts micro-gaps within a single GPU memory region by relocating only short-lived objects within that region using a two-phase fence and pointer-swap protocol to avoid global stops. We use per-region allocation bitmaps and hole-lists to guide compaction targets and a lightweight reservation API for continuous batching (fence-based reservations prevent reclamation of KV entries referenced by in-flight batches).
implementation_notes: Add per-GPU region metadata: age_counters, hole_bitmap, occupancy_histogram (low-dim) stored in host pinned memory for cheap readouts
Young reservoir: fixed-size micro-blocks (32B/64B/128B pools) to reduce internal fragmentation for token-level KVs
Promotion policy: sampled survivor count; default promote after 3 scavenger passes; tunable via runtime flags
Scavenger operation: runs on a dedicated CPU core per GPU, estimates cost budget per second and only compacts if budget available; uses CUDA memcpy async to relocate within same device

Fence/reservation API: batching layer registers KV references at request start; scavenger checks reservation epoch before relocating; pointer-swap uses atomic CAS on 64-bit descriptor to avoid-lock moves
Avoid expensive full object moves for large values: large KV entries are left in stable pool and reclaimed via existing eviction paths
Telemetry: expose fragmentation_ratio, promoted_bytes, compaction_operations, reservation_conflicts via /metrics and Console dashboards
testing_plan: Unit tests for reservation API and CAS-based pointer swap
Simulator test that injects mixed object lifespan distributions and validates no stale reads post-compaction
Load tests on dev-cluster with continuous-batching enabled and 8x A100 profile: baseline vs healed allocator
Safety tests: induce failures in mid-copy (GPU memcpy aborted) and verify roll-back path is safe and observable
migration_plan: Implement feature behind runtime flag runtime.kv.healing.enabled=false by default
Roll out to canary fleet (5%) with aggressive telemetry, enable automatic rollback on error budget breaches
Gradually increase to 25%, 50%, 100% with 24h observation windows and custom dashboards
rollout_steps: Merge gated feature branch + integration tests (PR link below)
Tweak promotion thresholds and scavenger budget based on telemetry
Full rollout and deprecation of hotfix workaround code
metrics: median request latency with healing on/off
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: scavenger steals CPU and degrades latency — mitigate by strict CPU budget and backoff when latency signals increase
Risk: mid-copy GPU memcpy failure could corrupt KV pointers — mitigate with two-phase commit and verification CRC; fall back to mark-and-evict pattern
Risk: promotion mis-tuning causes thrash — add conservative defaults and auto-rate-limiter for promotions
